tier_reason: Benchmark code is public and pinned: ctz/openssl-bench (82b86b22) for OpenSSL/BoringSSL and rustls admin/bench-measure.mk with the rustls-bench binary (target/release). The 2026-03-07 rustls.dev report states GCC 12.2.0, Clang 14.0.6, Rust 1.94.0, the build commands (OpenSSL ./Configure; make, BoringSSL cmake Release, rustls release build) and the CPU (Xeon E-2386G), so tier A holds; the 2023 aochagavia run also meets A.

corrections.workload: Single-core in-process TLS benchmark, rustls 0.23.37 (aws-lc-rs 1.16.0 provider) vs OpenSSL 3.6.1 and BoringSSL 30cd935: bulk transfer (TLS 1.2 AES-128-GCM, TLS 1.3 AES-256-GCM) send/receive MB/s, full handshakes (RSA and ECDSA, TLS 1.2/1.3, client and server) and resumed handshakes per second. Earlier 2023 run (aochagavia/rustls-bench-results, rustls 0.22.0 vs OpenSSL 3.2.0) adds ChaCha20 throughput and per-session memory.
corrections.claimed_speedup: 2026-03-07 report, rustls 0.23.37 vs OpenSSL 3.6.1: rustls is faster on every reported row. Full handshakes 1.32x-2.59x, e.g. TLS 1.2 RSA client 8,122.99 vs 3,186.87/s (2.55x), TLS 1.2 RSA server 2,835.45 vs 2,154.41/s (1.32x), TLS 1.2 ECDSA server 13,524.99 vs 5,226.96/s (2.59x), TLS 1.3 RSA server 2,357.36 vs 1,712.64/s (1.38x). Resumed handshakes 1.87x-3.20x (TLS 1.2 server 72,480.52 vs 22,647.1/s). Bulk transfer 1.11x-1.27x (TLS 1.2 AES-128-GCM receive 7,946.96 vs 7,129.43 MB/s; TLS 1.3 AES-256-GCM send 7,421.02 vs 5,844.35 MB/s). Ratios derived from page data. The older 2023 run (rustls 0.22.0 vs OpenSSL 3.2.0) was mixed: client full handshakes 1.93x (TLS 1.2, 4,991.73 vs 2,581.16/s) and 2.06x (TLS 1.3), resumed handshakes 1.56x-3.30x, but server full RSA handshakes 0.70x/0.73x, receive throughput 0.83x-0.93x, ChaCha20-Poly1305 0.56x-0.58x; peak memory 131,816 KiB vs 688,436 KiB for 10,000 TLS 1.3 sessions (-81%).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: 2026 report: GCC 12.2.0 and Clang 14.0.6, Rust 1.94.0. OpenSSL 3.6.1 built with default './Configure ; make -j12'; BoringSSL with 'CC=clang CXX=clang++ cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release'; rustls-bench run from target/release via admin/bench-measure.mk; openssl-bench harness 82b86b22 built from its makefile. 2023 run: same C/C++ toolchains, rustls built with 'cargo build -p rustls --release --example bench' (aws_lc_rs feature), jemalloc, openssl-bench harness CXXFLAGS -O2.
corrections.hardware: Intel Xeon E-2386G (AVX-512), 32GB, Debian 12 (Bookworm), bare metal, hyper-threading and dynamic frequency scaling disabled, performance governor
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers (rustls maintainers' own rustls.dev/perf reports) but fully pinned and reproducible. Single-core, single-machine benchmarks; ChaCha20 is absent from the 2026 table and was 0.56x-0.58x of OpenSSL in the 2023 run (OpenSSL AVX-512 path). rustls uses aws-lc-rs (AWS-LC) as its crypto provider, so primitive speed is largely AWS-LC's. BoringSSL still beats rustls on bulk send in the 2026 table (8,291.9 vs 8,133.85 MB/s TLS 1.2 AES-128-GCM). rustls is itself one of the three named baselines for this category (OpenSSL, BoringSSL, rustls), so this entry records rustls vs OpenSSL, not a project beating rustls. The original record's 2023 figures come from the aochagavia/rustls-bench-results README itself (not a bencher.dev summary), and its '131.8MB vs 688.4MB' is really 131,816 KiB vs 688,436 KiB.

notes: Valid catalog entry: rustls is a measurably faster alternative to OpenSSL, since the current tier-A report shows rustls 0.23.37 ahead of OpenSSL 3.6.1 on all 16 rows (1.11x-3.20x). Tag it as a category baseline so it is never shown as beating rustls. benchmark_url was switched to the newer, stronger 2026-03-07 report; the original 2023 numbers were verified correct except the memory units and the omitted server-side full-handshake loss (0.70x/0.73x).

tier_reason: Independent blog benchmark with public code (wtx-bench.tar.xz: assets/bench.sh, Cargo.toml deploy profile) and a stated CPU (Ryzen 9 5900X), but no rustc version and no OpenSSL version or build flags, so not A. It is not a peer-reviewed paper or well-known suite, so not B; it measures whole-process time rather than isolated handshake cost.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Whole-process handshake run time (hyperfine mean, lower is better), read from the page's SVG bar charts (derived from page data, about +/-0.01 ms): aws-lc-rs 1.38-6.71 ms vs OpenSSL 4.41-10.20 ms. aws-lc-rs is faster than OpenSSL in all 45 combinations, by 1.30x-3.44x (median about 2.95x), e.g. Ed25519 + X25519 + AES-128-GCM 1.38 vs 4.74 ms (3.44x), RSA-PSS-SHA384 + X25519 + AES-256-GCM 6.66 vs 8.68 ms (1.30x). With RSA-PSS-SHA384 certificates aws-lc-rs (6.4-6.7 ms) trails ring (4.9-6.5 ms) and Graviola (5.2-5.9 ms), matching the page text; with secp384r1 key agreement it is fastest or near-fastest.
corrections.workload: Whole-process wall time of one wtx-bench binary run (hyperfine -N, 10 warmup + 10 measured runs, mean): decode 3 PEM files, start a TCP server thread and a client thread, complete one TLS handshake, exit without application data. 36 builds (4 crypto backends aws-lc-rs/Graviola/ring/OpenSSL x 3 key agreements secp256r1/secp384r1/X25519 x 3 cipher suites) each run with 5 certificate types (ECDSA P-256, ECDSA P-384, Ed25519, RSA-PSS-SHA256, RSA-PSS-SHA384), inside the WTX project's pluggable crypto layer.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: wtx-bench Cargo.toml (in the page's wtx-bench.tar.xz): cargo build --profile deploy, which inherits release with opt-level=3, lto=true, codegen-units=1, panic='abort', debug-assertions and overflow-checks off. Exact rustc version not stated (Cargo.toml only sets rust-version = 1.96; wtx is built with its 'nightly' feature). OpenSSL version and build flags not stated; the author says OpenSSL's result may come from 'a missing compile flag'. bench.sh sets AWS_LC_SYS_USE_SYSTEM=0 (vendored AWS-LC build).
corrections.caveats: Single blog benchmark by the WTX author. Numbers exist only as SVG bar charts; values here were read from bar geometry (plotters output, about 0.01 ms per pixel). It times whole processes (process start, PEM decoding, loopback TCP, one handshake), not crypto alone. OpenSSL's near-constant 2-5 ms penalty in every combination suggests fixed init or integration overhead, and the author says the cause is unknown (compile flag, misconfiguration, openssl-sys, or OpenSSL itself). Only 10 runs per point; rustc and OpenSSL versions unstated. aws-lc-rs is Rust bindings over AWS-LC (github.com/aws/aws-lc, already catalogued), so the crypto speed shown is AWS-LC's.

notes: SVG values extracted successfully: aws-lc-rs beats OpenSSL in all 45 combos (1.30x-3.44x) in this whole-process benchmark, but the fixed OpenSSL offset makes this weak evidence of crypto speed. Overlaps the catalogued AWS-LC entry (same C core); the orchestrator may prefer to fold it into AWS-LC as the Rust binding. License corrected from the repo LICENSE SPDX line.
